body: **Avoid repeating the non-targeting indices in every `nt_cells` CRT cache entry.** Here, `fit_idxs` is `c(trt_idxs, all_nt_idxs)`, so the same control indices are retained separately for every target. [Replogle et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9380471/) report 585 non-targeting control gRNAs and median coverage of 171 cells per perturbation. Assuming similar coverage for controls gives approximately 100,000 control cells. Repeating their integer indices across roughly 10,000 targets would take about 4 GB. Please store the common control set once.

**Make the cache tests reach the low-MOI `nt_cells` path.** `make_mock_crt_object()` always imports with `moi = "high"`. `set_analysis_parameters()` then forces `control_group = "complement"`, even when the test passes `"nt_cells"`. Thus both iterations of the cache-reuse test run the complement workhorse, and the cache-transplant test does not test a transition between the two paths. Please add a low-MOI fixture, assert that it actually selects `nt_cells`, and check cold versus warm results and refitting after an incompatible cache is supplied.

**Add a short cache-maintenance note beside the cache helpers.** The existing function comments are helpful, but the cache lifecycle spans several files. Could you consolidate the key rules in one clearly labeled comment block here: what the cache stores and how it is keyed; which inputs make a fit valid (including the relevant cell membership and ordering); which changes require invalidation, distinguishing the response and gRNA caches; and why calibration bypasses the gRNA cache and CRT random draws must remain fresh? Please include brief pointers to the reset/writeback functions and the tests protecting these rules. Keep it focused on the invariants future contributors must preserve, with a reminder to update the note and tests when cache dependencies change. A short in-code note is sufficient.
